not_a_claim: Every expectation here was read from the pinned Path of Building checkout named in recorded_from. None of it is a gameplay measurement, and none of it is evidence that the engine models the live game patch. The set answers one question: does this engine still answer the way the engine these values were recorded from answered?

fixtures.why: The class the initial release covers. If its tree index moves, every saved build that names classId 8 means something else.
Ascendancy identity is the class index plus the ascendancy index, so an inserted ascendancy renames every later one.
A default weapon skill: present in any saved build that equips a quarterstaff, so an import depends on it resolving.
Configuration metadata the optimizer sets. A renamed variable is silently ignored by the engine, so its absence must be noticed here.
Which slots belong to a weapon set is the only weapon-set fact the slot table carries.
Recorded, not remembered. The first value written here was Quarterstaff and the fixture rejected it: upstream files this base under type Staff with subType Warstaff.
A floor, not an equality: upstream adds nodes between releases, and a catalog that lost most of the tree is a different failure from one that gained a few.

Availability alone cannot tell a renamed field from a changed formula. These are the engine's own answers for one fixed document, so a changed life-per-level or class base attribute shows up as a mismatch even when every entity is still present.
